newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Asian currencies take breather.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Asian currencies take breather.

text.p: Asian currencies appeared to have calmed down on Friday morning as the market digested Thailand's move to a managed float exchange rate system.
Activity on the baht was moderate with focus on the Bank of Thailand's reference rate, which was set below Thursday's level at 28.189 baht to the dollar.
"The (baht/dollar) trade is around yesterday's level. There is still not much movement in the market today," said one dealer at a local bank.
Differential between the offshore and onshore baht value was almost negligible.
At 0340 GMT, the baht was at 28.60/00 a dollar in the domestic market while the offshore baht was at 28.650/750.
"Baht went slightly lower (after the annoucement of the reference rate). But I don't think the market really looks at the reference rate at all in the offshore market," another dealer said.
Malaysian ringgit eased on profit-taking and fresh dollar bids by offshore players, dealers said.
At 0340 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5235/40 to a dollar against its opening around 2.5165.
"Dollar/ringgit is firming back and may test the 2.5250 resistance again later today," said a dealer with a large Malaysian bank. "Dollar bids are still out there."
Dealers said they heard a buyer seeking a price for $100 million.
But the rinngit remained defended at 2.5250 to the dollar, a level which Bank Negara seemed comfortable with, dealers said.
The central bank was believed to have sold around $100-150 million on Thursday.
Dealers said Bank Negara was also in the swap market amid talk speculators were building up long ringgit positions on the swaps ahead of a potential squeeze by the central bank.
Also, there was concern the central bank would impose some restriction on the ringgit forwards next week, which would effectively create a two-tier market.
The Indonesian rupiah was well-bid against the dollar amid rumours of a central bank intervention band widening.
One major local bank dealer said offshore operators were continuing to sell dollar on speculation of the band widening, but strong local support limited the downside.
"The dollar is well supported at the 2,430.5 level. Local operators are not really convinced of an imminent widening," he said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,430.00/1.00 at 0340 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,431.5/32.0. Tomorrow was at 2,430.0/30.5. There was no trading in value today due to a U.S. holiday.
Economists and treasurers were mixed over the reason for an immediate widening.

They said a wider band would allow Indonesia to be better prepared for external and internal shocks. But others said market pressure was not heavy and a widening would ultimately appreciate the rupiah which could be then affect exports.
Singapore dollar took a breather from recent bashing, underpinned by short-covering by various funds.
"The focus is still on ringgit/Sing crosses, which is on a consolidation mode. Today, the Singapore has been range trading at 1.4320/50 to the dollar," said a dealer with a U.S. bank.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik
